Social Service Camp for the MBBS Batch 2025 at Goji Village Concluded
Thursday, 12 February 2026
1890 Hits
The Social Service Camp (SSC) of the newly admitted MBBS 2025 batch was conducted at Goji village from 27 January to 9 February 2026, with the active participation of 100 MBBS students. This rural immersion program - a hallmark of Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences - aims to orient students to the social determinants of health and provide experiential learning through close engagement with the community.
“The focus of the camp is not merely on identifying illnesses but on understanding health within the broader framework of social determinants and inequity,” informed Dr Arjun Jakasania (Associate Professor of Community Medicine and In-Charge of Social Service Camp)." Each student was allotted five adopted families from the village. Students visited their families twice daily throughout the camp, building rapport and understanding their social, economic, cultural, and health contexts. These repeated interactions enabled students to appreciate how factors such as occupation, gender roles, education, income, access to services, addictions, and social norms influence health outcomes and health-seeking behaviour", he added.
The camp witnessed several student-led initiatives that encouraged community participation and health awareness. Activities included a school health fair for children, street plays addressing relevant social and health issues, a farmer health interaction session, elderly health engagement activities, a de-addiction awareness drive and a movie night with a social message. These initiatives provided students an opportunity to apply public health thinking in real-life settings while fostering dialogue with different sections of the community.
“The experience of spending a fortnight in a village has definitely given me a new perspective to look at health at large. Events such as a Rangoli competition, healthy dish competition, cultural night among others strengthened our bonding with the community. These programs created a platform for shared celebration, trust-building, and meaningful interaction between us and community members,” said an undergraduate from 2025 Batch.
Specialists from Kasturba Hospital visited the camp daily to follow up on the patients identified by the students. Departments including Orthopaedics, Surgery, Ophthalmology, Paediatrics, Dermatology, ENT, Medicine, Physiotherapy, Ayurveda, and Dental services, participated, along with the General OPD. Over 1,000 villagers benefited from these services during the camp period. Patients requiring further evaluation or advanced management were referred to Kasturba Hospital, ensuring continuity of care.
“Like each year, the most significant outcome of the camp remains the experiential learning acquired by students. Living in the village, interacting closely with families, and observing rural lifestyles allowed them to understand health inequities beyond textbooks. Students learned to listen, reflect, and recognise the complex interplay between social realities and medical conditions. They also experienced the importance of humility, patience, and community engagement in public health practice,” informed Dr Subodh Gupta (Head of Community Medicine, MGIMS)
“Our residential Social Service Camps are a platform designed for our young students for immersive learning, service, and mutual exchange of knowledge. While students experience rural life at close quarters, they also learn resilience, wisdom, and the realities of village life from the community. Our doctors and staff put in a lot of effort to ensure meaningful community-based learning for future doctors,” said Shri PL Tapadiya (President, Kasturba Health Society).
